correctness.rationale: The full proof constructs the correct Crofton dσ dt law and Gaussian isonormal representation (integrating offsets before averaging normals), reduces a generic section to edge splits k(m-k), obtains the exact expectation from Gaussian widths, controls the width tilt in L1 and obtains the bulk log exponent using Gaussian Mills tails and finite-grid uniformity. For each fixed a in (0,1/4), Gaussian empirical quantile convergence plus L2 uniform integrability proves the 2q_a offset-length limit; reciprocal chi-square concentration yields the rare probability and conditional marked law. All normalizations and boundaries match the statement. The embedded standard-library script passed 2,310 exact edge counts and supporting finite tests; numerics are not used as proof of limits.

value.rationale: Natural stochastic-combinatorial invariant of regular simplices with a sharp contrast between typical polynomial-order section complexity and its expectation. The continuously distributed exponent and explicit 1/sqrt(log m) rare-event constant, along with the conditional limit distribution, explain why quadratically complex sections dominate the mean even though typical sections are smaller. The result is a motivated universal high-dimensional law, not a finite exercise or a parametric rephrasing.
